focus: Angle 2 scoring: command projection population, lane weights, slash-only command keywords, plain-phrase boost coverage and the read-only/mutating confidence cliff
noveltyJustification: All 9 findings are new to the packet: iteration 1 counted bridges, this iteration traced the lane and projection mechanics that decide whether those bridges can ever be recommended.
keyQuestions: Why do plain planning and research prompts return zero recommendations, and what do the no-slash penalty and the mutating-command gate cost in recall versus what they buy in precision?

label: The TypeScript scorer holds 5 hand-authored command projections plus exactly 62 generated ones, of which 40 are routingEnabled true and 22 false, mirroring command-bridges.generated.json rather than forming a second inventory.
The JSON bridge inventory omits kind, routingEnabled and readOnly, while every generated projection carries them; the build-time generator knows what the human-readable inventory drops.

Command projections declare only slash strings as keywords and intentSignals — command-spec-kit declares exactly /speckit:plan, /speckit:resume, /deep:research and /deep:review — so the lexical and derived lanes cannot match a plain sentence against a command.

Plain chat reaches a command id only through the explicit lane PHRASE_BOOSTS table: 8 phrase rows naming 3 command families (create:agent, create:manual-testing-playbook, memory:save) out of roughly 100 rows, leaving 42 of 45 commands with no chat-only path.

A typed slash command is programmed to rank the owning skill above the bridge: /deep:research boosts system-deep-loop 1.6 and command-spec-kit 0.45, /speckit:resume boosts system-spec-kit 0.9 and command-spec-kit 0.75, so the typed path is a skill recommendation carrying a bridge id as a low-weight runner-up.
The explicit lane can also demote a bridge: after /speckit:resume it emits command-spec-kit at -1.0 with evidence speckit-resume-skill-disambiguation, deliberately removing the bridge from that path.

The mutating-command gate is a 0.57 confidence cliff controlled by one boolean: readOnlyRouteAllowed() lifts a command only when kind is command, readOnly is true and a keyword matches at phrase boundary; a gated route sits at floor 0.25 and an allowed one at 0.82.
Only 15 of 62 generated command projections carry readOnly true and all 15 are doctor routes, so the read-only lift is unreachable for 30 of the 45 commands even where a bridge exists.

Lane weights make prose-driven command recall structurally expensive: explicit_author 0.42 versus lexical 0.28, graph_causal 0.13, derived_generated 0.12 and semantic_shadow 0.05, and a prose command has empty keywords in the 0.28 lane while a typed command rides the 0.42 lane.

reason: No such constant exists; plain-chat command recall fails because command keywords are slash-only and PHRASE_BOOSTS covers 3 command families
